synopsis: Griffin appears as a co-author with Buehler and Ross of 1994 research documenting systematic underestimation of completion times for academic and non-academic tasks [f9598]. Chapter 12 and the glossary both report that only 29.7% of students finished their thesis by their own best-estimate date [f9599, f16311]. Underestimation persisted even when participants were instructed to be pessimistic, and participants focused on their current plan rather than relevant past outcomes [f9600, f9601, f16312]. The glossary rates the planning-fallacy finding as proven; the supplied facts are consistent but do not quantify its implications for the machine-validation project's schedule [f16312, f9598, f9599].

relations.note: Both report 29.7% thesis completion by students' best-estimate dates.
